questions.work_package: Premises, planning and property
questions.question: Can a home business or home industry run as exempt development in NSW, and on what conditions?
questions.answer: Yes, if the use meets the Standard Instrument definitions: the Codes SEPP lets a dwelling be used for a home business, home industry or home occupation as exempt development, with up to 2 non-resident employees, one sign up to 1 m², and the floor-area cap in the council LEP's clause 5.4 (no less than 30 m²). Exclusions (food manufacture, skin penetration, sex services) don't affect electronics.
questions.next_action: Read Dubbo LEP 2022 cl 5.4 for the exact m² figure; then ask Council planning to confirm the activity fits 'home business' (WP01-04).

questions.work_package: Legal entity, second-hand dealing, tax and privacy
questions.question: What does the second-hand dealer law exempt for recycling programs, and which regulation is current?
questions.answer: The regulation text found says the Act does not apply to conducting a recycling or rubbish collection program, selling goods collected in one, or contracting to give someone ownership of such goods. That text is in the Pawnbrokers and Second-hand Dealers Regulation 2021. NSW's staged repeal would have ended the 2021 Regulation around 1 September 2026, so a 2026 remake may now be current — other repo notes cite 'Regulation 2026'. Which instrument is in force wasn't confirmed.
questions.next_action: Check legislation.nsw.gov.au for a 2026 Regulation and compare the exemption wording; then ask Fair Trading in writing whether refurbish-and-sell of donated devices is a 'recycling program'.

questions.work_package: Legal entity, second-hand dealing, tax and privacy
questions.question: Can a licensed dealer wipe, test or repair goods during the retention period?
questions.answer: No alteration until the retention period ends, and goods must be kept on notified premises (NSW business obligations page). Fair Trading grants some licensees limited exemptions, including from retention where the seller already held the goods for the required period. Whether data wiping is 'alteration' isn't stated.
questions.next_action: If licensed, don't wipe during the hold; ask Fair Trading whether data erasure counts as alteration.

questions.work_package: Legal entity, second-hand dealing, tax and privacy
questions.question: Must second-hand electrical goods be tested, tagged or labelled before resale in NSW?
questions.answer: No NSW clause requiring test-and-tag or an 'untested' label for second-hand articles was found: Part 6 of the Gas and Electricity (Consumer Safety) Regulation covers safety-direction notices and disposal of non-conforming articles. NSW guidance says a second-hand declared article must have been approved when sold new, and sellers of second-hand electrical equipment have obligations to ensure it's safe. Queensland, by contrast, requires sellers to tell buyers if an item is untested.
questions.next_action: Only resell items with original compliance marks; run and record a safety check; disclose test status in listings as good practice. Check the current Regulation version for changes since 2020.

questions.work_package: Legal entity, second-hand dealing, tax and privacy
questions.question: Can second-hand e-bikes, e-scooters and their batteries be resold in NSW?
questions.answer: Not without testing, certification and marking: from 1 February 2026 e-micromobility devices and their lithium-ion batteries sold in NSW, including second-hand ones and former hire fleets, must be tested, certified and marked. They are now declared electrical articles.
questions.next_action: Exclude e-micromobility from intake and resale; add to INTAKE-POLICY reject list.

questions.work_package: Supply, institutional disposal and procurement
questions.question: How do the NSW and National Device Banks work, and can Dubbo organisations take part?
questions.answer: The NSW Device Bank launched in May 2026 as a 12-month pilot run by NSW Telco Authority with WorkVentures. It refurbishes surplus government laptops and distributes them, with Good Things Australia, through community organisations and charities in metro, regional and remote NSW; the first laptops went out by late July 2026. Community organisations apply through WorkVentures' EOI. The separate National Device Bank (WorkVentures and Good Things Australia) takes business and government donations, and reported in February 2026 that demand exceeded devices committed.
questions.next_action: Point a Dubbo charity partner at the WorkVentures EOI; Dubbo eWaste itself isn't the eligible applicant.

questions.work_package: Battery, electrical safety and WHS
questions.question: Does NSW's new battery stewardship regulation affect Dubbo eWaste?
questions.answer: The Product Lifecycle Responsibility Regulation 2026 commenced on 1 October 2026 as Australia's first mandatory battery stewardship scheme; obligations fall on brand owners, and with no Product Stewardship Organisation appointed yet, brand owners must comply individually. Whether a refurbisher that imports replacement batteries or supplies devices containing batteries is a 'brand owner' wasn't established.
questions.next_action: Ask NSW EPA whether buying replacement batteries from local suppliers (not importing) keeps Dubbo eWaste out of brand-owner obligations.

questions.work_package: Battery, electrical safety and WHS
questions.question: Does repairing plug-in devices need an electrical licence in NSW?
questions.answer: An electrical licence is needed for 'electrical wiring work' — physical work on an electrical installation. Older NSW definitions exclude appliances connected through a socket from the installation, and disconnecting or reconnecting hard-wired equipment needs its own certificate. So repairing plug-in laptops and power supplies isn't licensed wiring work (inference from definitions); general safety duties still apply.
questions.next_action: Don't open mains-side PSUs or hard-wired equipment; confirm with Building Commission NSW if in doubt.

questions.work_package: Battery, electrical safety and WHS
questions.question: What must a workplace do about lithium-ion incidents in NSW?
questions.answer: A PCBU must notify SafeWork NSW immediately on 13 10 50 of a serious injury, illness, death or dangerous incident caused by a lithium-ion battery; SafeWork, FRNSW, Fair Trading and the EPA publish joint charge/store/recycle guidance.
questions.next_action: Add the notification step to SAFETY-DECISION-TREES.md.

questions.work_package: Policy, funding, circular economy and impact
questions.question: Are there open grants that fit right now?
questions.answer: Nothing suitable is open. The EPA's Local Government Waste Solutions Fund is for councils in the waste-levy area (Round 4 closed October 2025; it funded a Port Macquarie reuse/repair event pilot) — Dubbo is likely outside the levy area (inference). The Environmental Trust's 2026 rounds have closed. The EPA's Together on Country program supports Aboriginal communities' circular-economy work and business partnerships and may fit a partnership. Dubbo's 2026/27 community funding closes 28 February 2027 (other session).
questions.next_action: Budget zero grant income; watch the EPA grants calendar.

The Productivity Commission's reuse/repair target recommendation for the NTCRS remains a recommendation.
